image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Keep the connector gripped; make a small lateral and pitch alignment correction while approaching slowly. Depth and plug-relative tilt remain uncertain.
Refine pitch using the opposed tactile edge slopes and center the plug over the visible slot; continue a millimeter-scale descent.
The plug is centered in the head view and retained in both tactile views. Lower vertically toward the socket, keeping the current alignment.
Approach the slot mouth with half-millimeter vertical steps and a tiny lateral centering adjustment; watch for contact or slipping.
The tip visually meets the slot mouth. Begin slow straight insertion while retaining the current grip and orientation.
Continue the centered insertion in quarter-millimeter increments, monitoring the tactile patches for relative movement.
Tactile contact has moved during descent, suggesting the plug may be resting on the rim. Relieve contact and make a small depth alignment correction rather than pushing farther.
Lift slightly to clear uncertain rim contact and check retention before further angular correction; modestly reduce the opening target.
The lifted tip is visibly clear and retained. Correct the residual pitch inferred from the tactile slopes, with a small lateral recentering.
With pitch corrected and the tip centered in the image, approach the socket vertically in small steps; monitor contact before further insertion.
The tip is at the rim without confirmed insertion. Lift clear and correct depth away from the camera, compensating for the fingertip displacement introduced by pitch alignment.
Complete a small depth correction while lowering toward the visible mouth. Preserve pitch and lateral centering, and check for relative plug motion.
Lower straight toward the slot mouth after the depth correction; the plug remains visibly retained and the gap is small.
Begin a gentle insertion from the apparent mouth contact. Watch tactile patch stability rather than relying on arm tracking alone.
The plug bottom stayed fixed while tactile contact shifted, indicating rim contact rather than insertion. Lift clear before reassessing the pitch sign and depth.
The connector is clear again. Try an intermediate depth between the two rim-contact approaches, maintaining the pitch suggested by the tactile geometry.
Test insertion at the intermediate depth with a one-millimeter descent, checking whether the plug advances or slips against the fingers.
Advance slowly at the current alignment. The contact patches appear largely stable, but seating is not yet confirmed.
The plug stopped advancing and the tactile patches shifted. Relieve rim contact, then move a few millimeters away from the camera to test depth alignment.
Test the revised depth with a gentle vertical insertion; compare plug advance and tactile patch displacement.
Tactile contact is stable at this depth, so continue the slow insertion; the socket can occlude the advancing tip.
The tactile patches shifted along the fingers during descent, so relieve contact and move another small step away from the camera to correct the remaining depth mismatch.
Reapproach vertically at the corrected depth; tactile contact has returned to its retained shape and the tip is just above the mouth.
Contact patches displaced again. Lift clear, then shift farther from the camera by a few millimeters; perspective suggests residual depth mismatch.
The tip is visibly clear and centered laterally. Reapproach the socket at the new depth with a two-millimeter controlled descent.
The stopped tip projects behind the socket mouth. Lift off contact, then move toward the camera and slightly right to correct the visible rim-contact offset.
Close the small visible gap at the corrected depth and lateral position; retain the plug orientation and monitor for rim-induced slip.
Probe a shallow additional insertion at the apparent slot center; distinguish tip occlusion from sustained slipping using both tactile views.
The contact patches shift and tilt under descent. Relieve the rim load and follow the indicated small depth correction away from the camera.
The relieved tactile edges are less distorted. Test a one-millimeter insertion at this depth, keeping lateral alignment and grip fixed.
Descent displaced the plug along the fingers. Lift off the rim and remove a small residual pitch, compensating hand translation to approximately preserve tip depth.
Lift enough to fully unload the tip. Make a small yaw and roll correction while preserving approximate tip centering; repeated rim contact means depth alone was insufficient.
Recenter the tip slightly right and close most of the visible gap with the corrected yaw and pitch; keep the grip unchanged.
Try a shallow straight insertion with the revised angular alignment. Stop escalating descent if the tactile patch slides again.
The plug appears to contact just in front of the slot and slides backward in the fingers. Unload it, then adjust depth two millimeters away and recenter slightly right.
Lower to the mouth after the two-millimeter depth correction; preserve the revised pitch and yaw and watch for stable tactile contact.
The tactile shift indicates shallow rim contact. Hold height and make a small depth sweep toward the camera to locate the opening without increasing downward load.
The depth sweep tilted the retained plug against a constrained tip. Undo that lateral load, relieve slightly, and center the plug a fraction left over the mouth.
Repeated rim contact persists despite nearly upright pitch. Unload the tip and try a small yaw correction while approximately preserving lateral tip centering.
Reapproach the mouth at the revised yaw and depth, using a small vertical descent and watching for relative slip.
The tip is at the mouth but seating remains uncertain. Make a shallow depth-centering sweep away from the camera, then test a very small descent without increasing load substantially.
The depth adjustment reduced tactile edge distortion. Try another slow millimeter of insertion while preserving the current angular alignment.
Repeated slip suggests an angular mismatch remains. Unload the tip, then test a larger opposite yaw correction while compensating the lateral tip shift.
Reapproach with the opposite yaw correction; stop short of sustained downward loading and inspect tactile stability.
The opposite yaw still causes axial slip. Unload, return toward the prior yaw, and shift depth slightly toward the camera before another centered approach.
Approach the rim, then make a fine depth sweep toward the camera with minimal descent to find the opening without large axial slip.
Make a submillimeter left/depth centering correction at shallow contact, then check whether a small vertical advance enters the slot.
Repeated depth probes have not seated the plug. Lift clear and test the opposite pitch direction, approximately pivoting about the tip; tactile image-axis sign is uncertain.
Continue the opposite-pitch alignment test above the rim, translating the hand to keep the tip approximately stationary. The plug remains retained.
Explore the opposite pitch interpretation while clear of the mouth, pivoting approximately about the connector tip. Retain the grip and inspect the resulting geometry.
Complete the alternate pitch alignment above the slot with approximate tip-pivot compensation. Check the plug and mouth before descending.
Close the visible gap at the alternate pitch and make a small depth recentering. This is an alignment test, not confirmed insertion.
Advance gently from the small remaining gap, keeping the alternate pitch fixed and checking for rim-induced tactile motion.
The contact patches remain stable at the mouth. Continue a shallow insertion and check whether the retained connector advances without sliding.
The alternate pitch shortens the visible plug face and still causes slip. Lift clear and return toward the upright interpretation, using a tip-centered pivot rather than another depth-only probe.
Finish restoring the near-upright pitch and remove a small visible lateral lean. Raise the tip clear while compensating the rotation-induced translation.
The restored pitch leaves a clear gap above the socket. Close most of that gap vertically with the updated lateral-lean correction, then inspect before pressing farther.
Center the tip a fraction to the right and close the remaining submillimeter gap, retaining the corrected pitch and roll.
Begin slow axial insertion from the centered mouth contact. Inspect both plug advance and tactile deformation before choosing the next correction.
Unload the rim and correct a possible remaining yaw mismatch. Keep the tip approximately centered with compensating lateral motion; pitch appears close to upright.
Test a shallow insertion with the revised yaw, keeping depth and lateral centering fixed and watching for tactile slip.
Tactile contact is stable at the mouth after the yaw change. Continue a slow axial advance and check whether the plug seats or begins sliding.
Relieve the observed axial slip, modestly reduce the opening target, and make a submillimeter depth correction toward the camera before reapproaching.
Lift clear of repeated rim contact and move the retained plug toward the camera for a fresh depth alignment with the revised yaw.
Test slow straight insertion at the revised depth. The tip is at the mouth; monitor whether contact settles versus continued sliding.
Contact remains largely stable after the depth correction. Continue another gentle millimeter while checking for sustained insertion rather than rim slip.
The connector visibly advanced with little tactile change. Continue slow straight insertion at the current alignment, without changing the grip.
The tactile patches shifted while the plug stopped advancing. Ease the load and correct depth one millimeter away from the camera, retaining the revised yaw.
Test a controlled shallow insertion after relieving the depth offset; retain the current grip and angular alignment and inspect the contact response.
The plug stayed at the rim while contact slid along the fingers. Relieve axial loading and correct its slightly forward depth position by two millimeters.
Lift fully clear to remove accumulated rim-induced tilt, then test a larger yaw correction with tip-centering compensation. Avoid continued sliding under load.
Close the visible gap at the new yaw while maintaining depth and lateral centering. Check the retained plug at the mouth before deeper insertion.
The tip is at the socket and tactile contact is stable. Test one millimeter of straight insertion at the revised yaw.
Try a further slow millimeter with a slight depth correction. The tip is occluded at the mouth; monitor whether tactile movement grows rather than assuming seating.
Relieve accumulated axial slip and refine depth by half a millimeter away from the camera before reapproaching. The narrow slot needs finer centering than prior probes.
Unload and bring yaw back near the socket's visible axis while shifting depth slightly away from the camera. Compensate lateral tip motion during the rotation.
Reapproach vertically at the refined depth and near-neutral yaw. Check whether the plug advances without sliding along the fingers.
Use a fine depth sweep away from the camera at shallow mouth contact, with minimal descent, to locate the narrow opening without further axial slip.
The depth sweep tilted the plug against a constrained tip. Reverse that lateral load toward the camera while slightly relieving contact, then reassess centering.
Unload the tip, center depth between the two opposite contact tilts, and refine yaw using the opposed tactile offsets while preserving tip centering.
Close the small gap with a submillimeter lateral recentering and slow vertical approach at the selected depth and yaw.
The tip has reached the mouth with stable tactile contact. Test another slow millimeter of insertion without changing alignment.
Unload the rim and correct yaw in the opposite direction indicated by the paired tactile offsets, with a small pitch refinement and approximate tip-pivot compensation.
Reapproach the mouth with the refined pitch and opposite yaw correction; retain the grip and monitor contact stability.
Test shallow insertion at the current alignment with a quarter-millimeter depth refinement; use tactile stability to distinguish seating from slip.
The tactile edges flatten under rim contact, indicating a depth-induced bend. Relieve slightly and shift toward the camera to restore the unloaded plug angle.
The contact slope has returned near its unloaded value. Test a slow insertion with a very small rightward centering adjustment.
Relieve the rim and remove a small residual forward pitch while approximately preserving the tip position. The present yaw appears consistent with the tactile offsets.
Test slow axial insertion with the refined pitch and yaw, keeping depth and lateral centering fixed while checking tactile displacement.
Relieve the shallow contact and shift depth slightly toward the camera to remove the tactile-indicated bend, then gently re-test the opening.
Continue the fine depth correction with only a half-millimeter axial advance, seeking the unloaded tactile angle at the socket mouth.
Depth-induced pitch is now nearly relieved, but opposed tactile offsets suggest residual yaw. Lift clear and rotate farther toward positive yaw with tip-centering compensation.
Reapproach the slot with the larger positive-yaw correction, preserving depth and grip while checking whether the tip advances without sliding.
Contact is stable after the approach. Test a gentle one-millimeter insertion at the current yaw, watching for plug advance versus axial slip.
The larger yaw still slips at the rim. Return to the smaller yaw, unload the tip, and modestly reduce gripper opening to retain the connector during a fresh approach.
Test a slow straight insertion with the reduced opening target, checking whether the connector advances rather than sliding.
The current tactile slope indicates residual forward lean. Correct that pitch by a small tip-centered pivot while relieving contact, rather than pressing farther.
The pitch pivot preserved the tactile contact while bringing the plug closer to upright. Test a slow straight insertion without further angular changes.
Axial slip persists despite the pitch correction. Relieve contact and test a one-millimeter lateral correction, which may be hidden by the coarse head-image alignment.
Lift the retained connector fully clear of the socket to remove accumulated slip and contact-induced tilt before measuring a fresh alignment.
Hold clear of the socket and restore the original opening target, allowing contact-induced distortion to relax while checking that the plug remains retained.
The plug is retained and contact has relaxed. Its current pitch, yaw, and lateral projection look aligned; begin a fresh straight approach from clear space.
Continue the fresh vertical approach while the tip is visibly clear; preserve the relaxed grip geometry and stop near the mouth for a contact check.
Close the remaining visible gap slowly, maintaining the present alignment and watching for the first tactile displacement at the rim.
The tip reached the mouth with stable tactile contact. Test a gentle one-millimeter insertion while keeping alignment and grip unchanged.
Tactile contact remains nearly unchanged despite tip occlusion at the socket. Continue a slow axial advance and watch for sustained slipping.
The connector slipped axially and appears slightly left of the socket center. Relieve contact while shifting one millimeter right, then reapproach gently.
Test a shallow straight insertion after lateral recentering, monitoring whether the connector advances or slips along the fingers.
Relieve the renewed axial slip and refine both pitch and yaw from the tactile edge geometry, compensating translation to preserve approximate tip centering.
Clear the tip and further correct the yaw suggested by the opposed tactile contact offsets, keeping pitch fixed and compensating lateral tip motion.
The connector is visibly clear and retained. Reapproach the mouth at the revised yaw, stopping near first contact for an alignment check.
Close the small remaining gap and test shallow insertion at the current angular alignment, watching for tactile slip rather than assuming seating.
Tactile contact remains stable at the mouth. Continue a gentle axial advance and check whether the plug advances without relative sliding.
Axial slip resumed at the rim. Lift clear and remove the small visible sideways lean, pivoting approximately about the tip while preserving depth and yaw.
Reapproach the mouth with the corrected sideways lean, keeping pitch, yaw, and depth fixed; inspect the contact before deeper insertion.
The tip is at the mouth and tactile contact is stable. Test a gentle one-millimeter insertion while monitoring plug motion relative to the fingers.
The tip is occluded at the mouth and the exposed body is shortening. Continue a controlled axial advance to test seating, monitoring whether tactile slip grows substantially.
Substantial axial contact displacement confirms obstruction rather than seating. Lift fully clear to reassess the relaxed connector orientation and position.
With the plug fully clear, correct its small visible sideways lean and residual pitch, approximately pivoting about the tip while maintaining lateral centering.
Close the visible gap with the freshly corrected orientation, keeping the grip and lateral alignment fixed; inspect at the socket mouth before deeper insertion.
